coarse_request: Please design a 'Farming Bot creation process' that includes the roles of 'player' and 'system'. The key activities are 'collect resource preferences' and 'start farming', and there should be decision points regarding 'resource dependencies' and 'milestone achievement'.
fine_grained_text:
Step 1: The process starts with an informational meeting among the web design team.
If this meeting is not successful, the process ends here.
Otherwise, the team starts by creating a storyboard.
After an agreement on the storyboard, part of the team starts working on the design and development of the website.
Simultaneously, the team will start to prepare an initial draft of the content.
In case a review of the draft is needed, the marketing team will conduct this, before the web design team creates the final version of the content.
When the development and content have been completed, the website will be built and reviewed.
If the site is approved, the process is completed, otherwise the team goes back to the building step.
[Transition]: **If the website is approved, the process transitions to a formal IT solution request to integrate the new site into the company’s infrastructure.**
Step 2: The process starts when an employee or department submits a request for an IT solution, such as new software or hardware.
IT assesses the request, checking for compatibility with existing systems and evaluating cost and resource needs.
If approved, IT procures the necessary tools or licenses, installs the solution, and tests it in a controlled environment.
After successful testing, the new solution is rolled out to the requesting department.
Training may be provided, and IT support remains available for troubleshooting.



Please design an IT solution request process that only includes the roles of 'employee or department' and 'IT'. The key activities are 'assess request' and 'procure and install solution', and there should be decision points regarding 'request approval' and 'successful testing'.
[Transition]: Upon successful testing and rollout of the new solution in Process A, the requestor initiates the B2B U-Turn implementation by submitting a NE Project Request to the 3rd Party Access Solutions Workgroup (3PASWG) to formally register the solution in the CCR.
Step 3: The Citigroup Inter-Corporation Business-to-Business (B2B) Network U-Turn Request workflow is as follows:
1. Requestors submit a NE Project Request for B2B U-Turn implementation.
2. The 3rd Party Access Solutions Workgroup (3PASWG) receives product order requests, analyzes requirements, and then assigns a network engineer.
3. 3PASWG notifies the requestor of B2B U-Turn implementation requirements and the CCR approval process. The requestor obtained business justification, a BISO statement of compliance, and a signed B2B U-Turn notification letter in the notification. At the same time, 3PASWG creates a high-level B2B U-Turn diagram for providing it to the requestor.
4. Requestors submit B2B U-Turn approval requests in CCR. The 3PASWG then reviews the request, and immediately thereafter, it refers the request to the Information Security Technology Group (ISTG) for review.
5. ISTG reviews the request and notifies the requester of rejection or approval, depending on its review. The process ends after rejection. If the review notifies the requestor of approval, the requestor receives an approval notification and notifies NE. After the requester is notified of the approval, the 3PASWG first proceeds with the design and implementation of the B2B U-Turn and then advises the requester to register the U-Turn in the CCR. The process ends when the requester registers a B2B U-Turn in CCR.
[Transition]: Once the B2B U-Turn is successfully implemented and registered in CCR, the organization can then schedule a compliance audit to verify that the new network architecture adheres to required regulatory standards.
Step 4: The process starts when a company schedules a compliance audit for regulations such as ISO standards, safety protocols, or environmental guidelines.
Internal teams prepare documentation, gather evidence, and conduct a self-assessment before the external audit.
Auditors review the company's processes and identify any gaps or issues.
After making the necessary corrections or improvements, the company undergoes a final audit.
If all criteria are met, the company is awarded certification, and the process concludes with the issuance of official documents.
[Transition]: Upon successful certification, the company must maintain compliance by actively monitoring for issues, which triggers Process B whenever a new incident is reported.
Step 5: This process begins when an employee or customer reports an incident, such as a technical issue or workplace safety concern.
The report is logged into a tracking system and assigned to the appropriate team for investigation.
The team gathers necessary information, identifies the cause of the incident, and proposes corrective actions.
The solution is implemented, whether it's a fix, training, or policy change.
After the incident is resolved, a follow-up occurs to ensure that the issue won't recur.
The process ends when the incident report is closed, and all stakeholders are notified.
[Transition]: The implementation of a corrective action from an incident report may require a formal IT solution, which initiates the request process.
Step 6: The process starts when an employee or department submits a request for an IT solution, such as new software or hardware.
IT assesses the request, checking for compatibility with existing systems and evaluating cost and resource needs.
If approved, IT procures the necessary tools or licenses, installs the solution, and tests it in a controlled environment.
After successful testing, the new solution is rolled out to the requesting department.
Training may be provided, and IT support remains available for troubleshooting.
[Transition]: Upon the successful deployment of the new IT solution, the requesting department utilizes the software to access the game's backend systems, thereby initiating the Farming Bot creation process.
Step 7: Title: Farming Bot

Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.
